title: The Doctrine of Justification: Westminster Confession Chapter 11
speaker: Elder Scott Hollander

outline.title: Defining Justification
subpoints: Justification is a one-time judicial act, not a process
It is an act of God's free grace, not owed to man
God pardons sin and accepts the sinner as righteous

outline.title: The Certainty of the Ordo Salutis
subpoints: Those effectually called are freely justified
The 'Golden Chain' of salvation in Romans 8
The logical progression from foreknowledge to glorification

outline.title: What Justification Is Not
subpoints: Not by infusing righteousness or making one holier
Not for anything wrought or done by the believer
Not by imputing faith or evangelical obedience as righteousness

outline.title: The Basis of Justification: Imputation
subpoints: Christ's obedience and satisfaction are imputed to the believer
The believer receives and rests on Christ by faith
Faith is the instrument, not the ground, of justification

outline.title: The Forensic Nature of the Doctrine
subpoints: Legal terminology: pardon, accept, account, impute
Contrast with transformative or infusion-based views
Paul's use of legal language in Romans

summary: This lesson, the third in a series on the Westminster Confession of Faith, examines Chapter 11 regarding the doctrine of justification. The teaching emphasizes that justification is a judicial act of God's free grace, wherein He pardons the sins of the elect and accepts them as righteous. This status is not achieved through moral transformation or the infusion of righteousness, but solely through the imputation of Christ's perfect obedience and satisfaction to the believer.
